From 10bc6a6042c900934a097988b5d50e3cf3f91781 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Heiner Kallweit <hkallweit1@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Sep 2018 22:47:09 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] r8169: fix autoneg issue on resume with RTL8168E

It was reported that chip version 33 (RTL8168E) ends up with
10MBit/Half on a 1GBit link after resuming from S3 (with different
link partners). For whatever reason the PHY on this chip doesn't
properly start a renegotiation when soft-reset.
Explicitly requesting a renegotiation fixes this.

Fixes: a2965f12fde6 ("r8169: remove rtl8169_set_speed_xmii")
Signed-off-by: Heiner Kallweit <hkallweit1@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Neil MacLeod <neil@nmacleod.com>
Tested-by: Neil MacLeod <neil@nmacleod.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/realtek/r8169.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/realtek/r8169.c
index bb529ff2ca81..ab30aaeac6d3 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/realtek/r8169.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/realtek/r8169.c
@@ -4071,6 +4071,15 @@ static void rtl8169_init_phy(struct net_device *dev, struct rtl8169_private *tp)
 	phy_speed_up(dev->phydev);
 
 	genphy_soft_reset(dev->phydev);
+
+	/* It was reported that chip version 33 ends up with 10MBit/Half on a
+	 * 1GBit link after resuming from S3. For whatever reason the PHY on
+	 * this chip doesn't properly start a renegotiation when soft-reset.
+	 * Explicitly requesting a renegotiation fixes this.
+	 */
+	if (tp->mac_version == RTL_GIGA_MAC_VER_33 &&
+	    dev->phydev->autoneg == AUTONEG_ENABLE)
+		phy_restart_aneg(dev->phydev);
 }
 
 static void rtl_rar_set(struct rtl8169_private *tp, u8 *addr)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/net/ethernet/realtek/r8169.c`**
- Added a conditional block in the `rtl8169_init_phy` function to explicitly request a renegotiation of the PHY link after a soft reset. This is specifically for chip version 33 (RTL8168E) when it is detected that the device is in autonegotiation mode.
- The added comments explain the issue where the chip ends up with a 10MBit/Half link after resuming from S3 and how the explicit renegotiation resolves this problem.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a specific bug reported for the RTL8168E chip version 33, which was identified in the context of a previous commit (a2965f12fde6) that removed the `rtl8169_set_speed_xmii` function. The new code ensures that the PHY properly renegotiates the link speed after a soft reset, thereby fixing the autonegotiation issue that arises after the system resumes from a low-power state (S3).

Here is the commit message:
r8169: fix autoneg issue on resume with RTL8168E

It was reported that chip version 33 (RTL8168E) ends up with
10MBit/Half on a 1GBit link after resuming from S3 (with different
link partners). For whatever reason the PHY on this chip doesn't
properly start a renegotiation when soft-reset.
Explicitly requesting a renegotiation fixes this.

Fixes: a2965f12fde6 ("r8169: remove rtl8169_set_speed_xmii")
Signed-off-by: Heiner Kallweit <hkallweit1@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Neil MacLeod <neil@nmacleod.com>
Tested-by: Neil MacLeod <neil@nmacleod.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug is that the PHY on the RTL8168E chip version 33 does not properly initiate a renegotiation of the link speed after a soft reset when the device resumes from a low-power state (S3). As a result, the device incorrectly defaults to a 10MBit/Half link instead of the expected 1GBit link, leading to connectivity issues.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void rtl8169_init_phy(struct net_device *dev, struct rtl8169_private *tp)
 {
 	rtl_hw_phy_config(dev);
 
 	if (tp->mac_version <= RTL_GIGA_MAC_VER_06) {
 		netif_dbg(tp, drv, dev,
 			  "Set MAC Reg C+CR Offset 0x82h = 0x01h\n");
 		RTL_W8(tp, 0x82, 0x01);
 	}
 
 	pci_write_config_byte(tp->pci_dev, PCI_LATENCY_TIMER, 0x40);
 
 	if (tp->mac_version <= RTL_GIGA_MAC_VER_06)
 		pci_write_config_byte(tp->pci_dev, PCI_CACHE_LINE_SIZE, 0x08);
 
 	if (tp->mac_version == RTL_GIGA_MAC_VER_02) {
 		netif_dbg(tp, drv, dev,
 			  "Set MAC Reg C+CR Offset 0x82h = 0x01h\n");
 		RTL_W8(tp, 0x82, 0x01);
 		netif_dbg(tp, drv, dev,
 			  "Set PHY Reg 0x0bh = 0x00h\n");
 		rtl_writephy(tp, 0x0b, 0x0000); //w 0x0b 15 0 0
 	}
 
 	/* We may have called phy_speed_down before */
 	phy_speed_up(dev->phydev);
 
 	genphy_soft_reset(dev->phydev);
+
+	/* It was reported that chip version 33 ends up with 10MBit/Half on a
+	 * 1GBit link after resuming from S3. For whatever reason the PHY on
+	 * this chip doesn't properly start a renegotiation when soft-reset.
+	 * Explicitly requesting a renegotiation fixes this.
+	 */
+	if (tp->mac_version == RTL_GIGA_MAC_VER_33 &&
+	    dev->phydev->autoneg == AUTONEG_ENABLE)
+		phy_restart_aneg(dev->phydev);
 }

The call to `genphy_soft_reset` does not trigger the expected renegotiation, causing the device to default to a 10MBit/Half link instead of the required 1GBit link.

The code statements that fix the bug are:


The addition of the `phy_restart_aneg` function explicitly requests a renegotiation of the link speed after the soft reset. This ensures that the PHY correctly negotiates the link speed to 1GBit, resolving the connectivity issues experienced after resuming from S3.
